Release reports distinguish G1 evidence from later domain/procedure/compaction extension gates; never turn a synthetic specification check into product acceptance.
packages.title: Release

G1.extension_rule: Memory and cross-domain work do not block the coding product. AT22 applies to coding proposed/observed state using WP07; WP09 supplies later temporal-memory coverage. AT23 and AT25 are extension gates, not G1 gates.

G2.extension_rule: Require document evidence plus one numerical adapter. PSE and recurrent experiments remain optional choices within WP10.

G3.extension_rule: Also requires held-out policy-promotion benefit and regression evidence; package completion alone does not establish G3. Domain portability AT23 requires the separate G2/domain evaluation route; it is not implied by policy improvement on the coding domain.

rule: No package is complete without its named artifacts and passed acceptance evidence; no fixed calendar dates are promised. Optional PSE must not block the G1 coding slice. For each release, required_acceptance_ids selects applicable portions of package scope; extension-only acceptance must not silently become a G1 prerequisite.
